content_text_body:
People with a Growth Mindset (versus a Fixed Mindset) believe that their intelligence, skills and talents can improve through hard work, new experiences, challenges, and even failures. Teams who develop a growth mindset tend to learn and grow at a faster rate than others.

To get started, read this article on [Growth Mindset](https://hbr.org/2016/01/what-having-a-growth-mindset-actually-means).

### Reprogram mindset triggers 

As a group, identify triggers that work against a Growth Mindset. What skills has the team struggled to acquire? Where has the team performed poorly in the past? What tasks are very stressful for the team? 

### Shift your perspective

After identifying these mindset triggers, shift your team's perspective by discussing how each of these challenges can be opportunities to grow and improve. Give each other the permission to take risks, knowing that not all risks will work out.

### Build learning habits

Use what you learned the next time the team makes a mistake. Immediately get together to write down 3 things that can be learned from it. And for every instance where the team learned something new or improved, take a moment to celebrate -- even if a project did not meet its original goals.
